Coup, for 15-card play with 3 to 5 players. The deck holds 3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador and Contessa. Lose all your cards and you are out; the last player with a hidden card wins.

Coup: pay 7, the target loses a card, cannot be challenged or blocked; with 10 or more coins you must coup. Tax (claims Duke): +3. Assassinate (claims Assassin): pay 3 at once, the target loses a card; the target may block as Contessa. Steal (claims Captain): take 2 coins from the target (or all they have if fewer); the target may block as Captain or Ambassador. Exchange (claims Ambassador): draw 1 card from the deck, then return 1 hidden card. Costs are never refunded.

All other living players answer the action at the same moment: pass, challenge (only against a claimed role), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger after the active player counts. If the claim was true the claimer reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a replacement, and the challenger loses a card; if false the claimer loses a card and the action fails. If the action goes ahead and someone blocked, only the first blocker after the active player counts; everyone else answers accept or challenge, resolved the same way (a true block stops the action, a false block loses a card and the action goes ahead). Losing a card with two hidden means choosing one to reveal; losing as many cards as you hold eliminates you and your coins leave the game.

If 40 turns pass without a winner, the player with the most hidden cards wins, then the most coins; a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free talk.

Coup, for 15-card play with 3 to 5 players. The deck holds 3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador and Contessa. Each player is dealt 2 hidden cards that only they see; the first player starts with 1 coin and everyone else with 2. A revealed card is face up, public and permanent. Lose all your cards and you are out; the last player with a hidden card wins.

On your turn choose one action. Income: +1. Foreign Aid: +2, cannot be challenged, any other player may block it as Duke. Coup: pay 7, the target loses a card, cannot be challenged or blocked; with 10 or more coins you must coup. Tax (claims Duke): +3. Assassinate (claims Assassin): pay 3 at once, the target loses a card; the target may block as Contessa. Steal (claims Captain): take 2 coins from the target (or all they have if fewer); the target may block as Captain or Ambassador. Exchange (claims Ambassador): draw 1 card from the deck, then return 1 hidden card. Costs are never refunded.

All other living players answer the action at the same moment: pass, challenge (only against a claimed role), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger after the active player counts. If the claim was true the claimer reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a replacement, and the challenger loses a card; if false the claimer loses a card and the action fails. If the action goes ahead and someone blocked, only the first blocker after the active player counts; everyone else answers accept or challenge, resolved the same way (a true block stops the action, a false block loses a card and the action goes ahead). Losing a card with two hidden means choosing one to reveal; losing as many cards as you hold eliminates you and your coins leave the game.

If 40 turns pass without a winner, the player with the most hidden cards wins, then the most coins; a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free talk.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

You start with: You are seat 2. coins 2, hidden_cards ['Captain', 'Assassin']. you know seat 1 coins 1; seat 3 coins 2; seat 4 coins 2. action_status going, active_seat 1, assassinate_cost 3, block_challenger 0, blocker 0, challenger 0, copies_per_role 3, coup_cost 7, deck_count 7, deck_size 15, exchange_draw 1, exchange_return 1, first_player_start_coins 1, forced_coup_threshold 10, foreign_aid_gain 2, hand_size 2, income_gain 1, living_count 4, loss_per_hit 1, other_player_start_coins 2, steal_amount 2, target 0, tax_gain 3, turn_cap 40, turn_count 0, winner . still playing: 1, 2, 3, 4.

Each round runs in this order: start of turn → the state → the table → the action → the target → declare the action → reactions → action challenge → block responses → block and effect → which card to reveal → which card to return → resolve → decide the result → end check → next seat.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_action   answer with one of the options you are given
  the_target   answer with one seat number, from the list you are given
  reactions    answer with one of the options you are given
  block_responses answer with one of: accept, challenge
  which_card_to_reveal answer with one of the options you are given
  which_card_to_return answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

You are the referee of a turn-based game. You are not a player and you never speak to one. You are shown the complete state of the table, including information the players cannot see, and asked to produce one thing.

Answer only from the state you are given. Do not guess at anything not shown, do not reason about what a player is likely to do next, and do not soften a clear answer. If the state does not settle the question, say so by answering false or by returning nothing usable, rather than inventing an answer.

THE GAME
Coup, for 15-card play with 3 to 5 players. The deck holds 3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador and Contessa. Each player is dealt 2 hidden cards that only they see; the first player starts with 1 coin and everyone else with 2. A revealed card is face up, public and permanent. Lose all your cards and you are out; the last player with a hidden card wins.

On your turn choose one action. Income: +1. Foreign Aid: +2, cannot be challenged, any other player may block it as Duke. Coup: pay 7, the target loses a card, cannot be challenged or blocked; with 10 or more coins you must coup. Tax (claims Duke): +3. Assassinate (claims Assassin): pay 3 at once, the target loses a card; the target may block as Contessa. Steal (claims Captain): take 2 coins from the target (or all they have if fewer); the target may block as Captain or Ambassador. Exchange (claims Ambassador): draw 1 card from the deck, then return 1 hidden card. Costs are never refunded.

All other living players answer the action at the same moment: pass, challenge (only against a claimed role), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger after the active player counts. If the claim was true the claimer reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a replacement, and the challenger loses a card; if false the claimer loses a card and the action fails. If the action goes ahead and someone blocked, only the first blocker after the active player counts; everyone else answers accept or challenge, resolved the same way (a true block stops the action, a false block loses a card and the action goes ahead). Losing a card with two hidden means choosing one to reveal; losing as many cards as you hold eliminates you and your coins leave the game.

If 40 turns pass without a winner, the player with the most hidden cards wins, then the most coins; a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free talk.

Answer only from the state you are given. Do not guess at anything not shown, do not reason about what a player is likely to do next, and do not soften a clear answer. THE GAME
Coup, for 15-card play with 3 to 5 players. The deck holds 3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador and Contessa. Each player is dealt 2 hidden cards that only they see; the first player starts with 1 coin and everyone else with 2. A revealed card is face up, public and permanent. Lose all your cards and you are out; the last player with a hidden card wins.

On your turn choose one action. Income: +1. Foreign Aid: +2, cannot be challenged, any other player may block it as Duke. Coup: pay 7, the target loses a card, cannot be challenged or blocked; with 10 or more coins you must coup. Tax (claims Duke): +3. Assassinate (claims Assassin): pay 3 at once, the target loses a card; the target may block as Contessa. Steal (claims Captain): take 2 coins from the target (or all they have if fewer); the target may block as Captain or Ambassador. Exchange (claims Ambassador): draw 1 card from the deck, then return 1 hidden card. Costs are never refunded.

All other living players answer the action at the same moment: pass, challenge (only against a claimed role), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger after the active player counts. If the claim was true the claimer reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a replacement, and the challenger loses a card; if false the claimer loses a card and the action fails. If the action goes ahead and someone blocked, only the first blocker after the active player counts; everyone else answers accept or challenge, resolved the same way (a true block stops the action, a false block loses a card and the action goes ahead). Losing a card with two hidden means choosing one to reveal; losing as many cards as you hold eliminates you and your coins leave the game.

If 40 turns pass without a winner, the player with the most hidden cards wins, then the most coins; a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free talk.

You are the referee of a turn-based game. You are not a player and you never speak to one. You are shown the complete state of the table, including information the players cannot see, and asked to produce one thing.

Answer only from the state you are given. Do not guess at anything not shown, do not reason about what a player is likely to do next, and do not soften a clear answer. If the state does not settle the question, say so by answering false or by returning nothing usable, rather than inventing an answer.

THE GAME
Coup, for 15-card play with 3 to 5 players. The deck holds 3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador and Contessa. Each player is dealt 2 hidden cards that only they see; the first player starts with 1 coin and everyone else with 2. A revealed card is face up, public and permanent. Lose all your cards and you are out; the last player with a hidden card wins.

On your turn choose one action. Income: +1. Foreign Aid: +2, cannot be challenged, any other player may block it as Duke. Coup: pay 7, the target loses a card, cannot be challenged or blocked; with 10 or more coins you must coup. Tax (claims Duke): +3. Assassinate (claims Assassin): pay 3 at once, the target loses a card; the target may block as Contessa. Steal (claims Captain): take 2 coins from the target (or all they have if fewer); the target may block as Captain or Ambassador. Exchange (claims Ambassador): draw 1 card from the deck, then return 1 hidden card. Costs are never refunded.

All other living players answer the action at the same moment: pass, challenge (only against a claimed role), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger after the active player counts. If the claim was true the claimer reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a replacement, and the challenger loses a card; if false the claimer loses a card and the action fails. If the action goes ahead and someone blocked, only the first blocker after the active player counts; everyone else answers accept or challenge, resolved the same way (a true block stops the action, a false block loses a card and the action goes ahead). Losing a card with two hidden means choosing one to reveal; losing as many cards as you hold eliminates you and your coins leave the game.

If 40 turns pass without a winner, the player with the most hidden cards wins, then the most coins; a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free talk.

You are the referee of a turn-based game. You are not a player and you never speak to one. You are shown the complete state of the table, including information the players cannot see, and asked to produce one thing.

Answer only from the state you are given. Do not guess at anything not shown, do not reason about what a player is likely to do next, and do not soften a clear answer. If the state does not settle the question, say so by answering false or by returning nothing usable, rather than inventing an answer.

THE GAME
Coup, for 15-card play with 3 to 5 players. The deck holds 3 each of Duke, Assassin, Captain, Ambassador and Contessa. Each player is dealt 2 hidden cards that only they see; the first player starts with 1 coin and everyone else with 2. A revealed card is face up, public and permanent. Lose all your cards and you are out; the last player with a hidden card wins.

On your turn choose one action. Income: +1. Foreign Aid: +2, cannot be challenged, any other player may block it as Duke. Coup: pay 7, the target loses a card, cannot be challenged or blocked; with 10 or more coins you must coup. Tax (claims Duke): +3. Assassinate (claims Assassin): pay 3 at once, the target loses a card; the target may block as Contessa. Steal (claims Captain): take 2 coins from the target (or all they have if fewer); the target may block as Captain or Ambassador. Exchange (claims Ambassador): draw 1 card from the deck, then return 1 hidden card. Costs are never refunded.

All other living players answer the action at the same moment: pass, challenge (only against a claimed role), or block where allowed. Only the first challenger after the active player counts. If the claim was true the claimer reveals it, shuffles it into the deck and draws a replacement, and the challenger loses a card; if false the claimer loses a card and the action fails. If the action goes ahead and someone blocked, only the first blocker after the active player counts; everyone else answers accept or challenge, resolved the same way (a true block stops the action, a false block loses a card and the action goes ahead). Losing a card with two hidden means choosing one to reveal; losing as many cards as you hold eliminates you and your coins leave the game.

If 40 turns pass without a winner, the player with the most hidden cards wins, then the most coins; a remaining tie is a draw. There is no free talk.
